q: The de Rham cohomology H^k_{dR}(M) of a smooth manifold M is defined using differential forms. The de Rham theorem states:
opts: H^k_{dR}(M) ≅ H^k_{sing}(M; ℝ) (de Rham cohomology equals singular cohomology with real coefficients)
exp: de Rham's theorem: H^k_{dR}(M) ≅ H^k_{sing}(M;ℝ) via integration of k-forms over k-cycles. This profound theorem connects differential geometry (forms) to algebraic topology (singular cohomology), proved using the Mayer-Vietoris sequence and the Poincaré lemma.
